comment: Text recognition on the phone's GPU (OcrBridge, PP-OCR on LiteRT) for the Linux side's computer use, agent/computer-use/typesafe/linux_ocr.py, over the platform bridge's socket ($RUNGIC_PLATFORM_SOCKET). Framing: one JSON request line, followed by exactly `bytes` raw bytes, the RGB pixels row by row (bytes = width * height * 3, sides up to OcrBridge.MAX_SIDE); one JSON reply line: lines (text, score, box [x1, y1, x2, y2] in the image's pixels) and ms (timings), or {"error": string}, which the consumer answers by reading the text on the Linux CPU instead (also while the app is still downloading its models: available false, downloading). det_scale scales the detector's input (the consumer sends 1.5 image pixels per screen point at most 1); proxy is the Linux side's https proxy for that download. Recognizing an image changes nothing the user sees (it runs on the GPU in the app); an app without models starts their download on the first request, as the consumer's first use would. Tested from both ends: tools/tests/test_contract_ocr.py (linux_ocr.py against tools/contracts.py's stand-in) and acceptance scenario contract.ocr (a blank 64x32 image on the phone).
